title: Browser native capabilities lab
lead1: Many needs require no library at all: fullscreen, screen wake lock, geolocation, notifications, sharing, and network detection are all built into the browser. Here they are wrapped into Hooks, uniformly exposing a
lead2: field — when unsupported, it gives a clear explanation instead of doing nothing on click. The capability-detection logic lives in
lead3: as pure functions, covered by unit tests.
capTitle: Capability detection for the current browser
capHint: Results vary by browser: Safari added Wake Lock late, Network Information is mostly Chromium, and geolocation & clipboard require a secure context (HTTPS or localhost).
fsTitle: ① Fullscreen: put any element fullscreen
fsExitHint: Press Esc or click the button again to exit
fsEnterHint: Click the button below to fullscreen this area
wakeHint: Great for demo walls, monitoring dashboards, and recordings. When you switch tabs the browser auto-releases the lock, and returning to the foreground requires requesting it again.
wakeUnsupported: This browser does not support Screen Wake Lock (older Safari / insecure context)
geoHint: The browser pops an authorization prompt; denial or a non-HTTPS context both fail. The error is passed straight back, not silently swallowed.
geoUnsupported: Geolocation is unsupported in this environment
notifyBody: This is a native browser notification
notifyHint: Permission has three states: granted / denied / prompt. After denial you can only guide the user to change it in browser settings; code can no longer pop the prompt.
shareVibHint1: Share and vibrate are mostly unavailable on desktop (
shareVibHint2: will be false); they work best on mobile.
netTitle: ⑥ Network info: degrade loading by connection speed
netUnsupportedHint: This browser does not support the Network Information API (mostly Chromium).
netScenario: Practical use: on weak networks (2g / saveData), auto-degrade to low-res images, disable autoplay, and defer non-critical requests.
